senses.en_definition: To make or prepare something for someone.

collocations.en: prepare a drink for one's younger sibling
make a shirt for one's child

senses.en_definition: To cause someone to feel, experience, or do something.

messages.en: I got that scholarship! Next semester's tuition fees are covered.
Thank goodness. That's such a relief. I thought you'd have to put your studies on hold.
I'm relieved too. I can finally get a good night's sleep tonight.

senses.en_definition: To open something that is closed or covered.
To take off clothing, footwear, or other items worn on the body.
To untie or loosen a knot or binding.
To unfold, spread out, or open up something folded or closed.
(Colloquial) To switch on a light, appliance, or other electrical device.
To clear land for cultivation or development, or make a path or road.
To create or provide opportunities or scope for something.
To start an activity or meeting, or establish a business.
To reveal or expose something hidden or secret.
To stimulate an appetite or arouse a desire to do something.
To formally declare a building, facility, or event open.
To allow the public or a particular group to enter, attend, or participate.

collocations.en: open an exhibition to the public

messages.en: I heard Kak Ina's planning to open a breakfast place in our neighbourhood. Is that true?
Yeah, she starts serving next week. Let's go on Monday. Then we won't have to cook that morning.

collocations.en: prove that a claim is true
demonstrate the effectiveness of a method

messages.en: Have you paid yet? The money hasn't come through on my end.
I have. This receipt proves I've paid. Could you check again?

senses.en_definition: To cause a person or other living organism to die.
To extinguish, destroy, or eliminate something, such as enthusiasm or confidence.

messages.en: Amir failed maths again. I feel like just telling him, 'Your older brother can pass. Why can't you?'
Don't compare them like that. If you keep telling him he can't do it, you'll end up destroying his confidence.
You've got a point. Tonight I'll start by asking him which parts he's finding difficult.
